population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. Arithmetic: ever 21 − current 14.8 = 6.2% of adults used and are off now; 38% of ever-users (≈8.0% of adults) have stopped and restarted at least once, of whom ≈6.5 pts are on now and ≈1.5 pts have stopped again; so ever-stopped ≈ 6.2 + 6.5 = 12.7 pts (60% of ever-users, consistent with ~35% one-year persistence), and current users = 8.3 never-stopped/new + 6.5 restarters = 14.8. Age bands weighted by adult population shares (20/33/24/23%) give 1.4 + 4.6 + 5.8 + 3.0 ≈ 14.8. The 65+ rise (9→13) is Medicare coverage; the 50–64 band stays the peak. About 1.9 pts of current users (~5M adults) have BMI under 27 and take it for 'metabolic health' or longevity, mostly on cash-pay orals and mostly from the top income third; that use explains most of the gap between the top third and the middle. The bottom third is the most likely to be off-drug after a coverage loss: about half of its ever-users are off now, against about a quarter in the top third. Never-users, 79% of adults, include most adults with obesity in the bottom income third. Pediatric: 0.7% of under-18s (≈500k), almost all 12–17 on semaglutide or liraglutide; under-12 use is still specialist-only and still skews upper-income.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ended Dec 2027 as scheduled. CMMI replaced it in Jan 2028 with the Metabolic Outcomes Model: Medicare pays $245/month, beneficiaries still pay $50, and coverage continues past month 6 only if the patient has lost ≥5% of body weight or shows a comorbidity improvement, has ≥80% refill adherence (proportion of days covered) and logs a quarterly weight at a pharmacy or by connected scale. About 2.6M beneficiaries are enrolled for obesity. Spend: 2.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.6B a year federal, which fits inside CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 only because about 30% of enrollees drop out or fail the 6-month gate. Diabetes use continues under ordinary Part D. Fourteen state Medicaid programmes cover obesity at the same $245 rate, most with the same conditioning rules. TRICARE covers active-duty service members through the DoD readiness programme.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 60+ generic brands at $6–40/month. Canada's generics now run CAD 70–100/month. Brazil, Mexico and much of the Gulf have local generics. Generic semaglutide is sold in ~170 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32, and personal importation of Indian generics is a small, visible leak that the FDA tolerates rather than prosecutes.
access.note: Managed decline: cash prices through TrumpRx and the manufacturers' direct channels are $149 for starter-dose orals (Wegovy pill, Foundayo), $199–249 for semaglutide and tirzepatide pens, and $349 for retatrutide (Lilly agreed this launch price in exchange for Medicare formulary placement). List prices (Wegovy $1,349) are nominal. Of the 52% of large employers covering weight management (down from 60%), about 70% now attach conditions: enrolment in a vendor 'metabolic programme', weigh-ins, refill adherence, and a premium surcharge of up to 30% under HIPAA outcomes-based wellness rules for members who drop out. The 503B exclusion was finalised in 2027, so compounded product is now marginal. The wellness and longevity market runs mostly on $149 branded orals prescribed off-label by telehealth. Weekly injectables still lead by volume (~55% of fills), and orals have reached ~40%.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved 2027)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: knee osteoarthritis pain with obesity (retatrutide label, from its TRIUMPH programme)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' / longevity use by people with BMI under 27, mostly low-dose orals via telehealth (~5M adults)
low-dose 'calm' or 'quiet' protocols marketed for focus and freedom from craving
alcohol reduction (an sNDA for alcohol use disorder with obesity is under FDA review; not approved)
nicotine and gambling craving reduction (observational evidence only)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide BLA filed Feb 2027 and approved Mar 2028, 13 months after filing: 28.3% mean loss at 80 weeks, up to ~30% in BMI≥35. It is the 'surgical-grade' pen, but its label carries dysesthesia and its uptake is limited to ~0.6M users by the end of 2028 by supply ramp-up and prior authorisation. CagriSema was approved in 2027 and holds a niche. Survodutide was filed in mid-2027 and is under review. Amycretin's NDA was filed in Nov 2028, so it cannot be approved before late 2029. MariTide (monthly) remains in phase 3 and is not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle-preserving adjuncts are in phase 3. The global incretin market is ~$110B in 2028.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are higher on retatrutide at escalation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; the gastroparesis caution is retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss, and a larger concern with the ~28% losses on retatrutide.
Absolute risk is low and long-term RCT data still do not establish causation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Multidistrict litigation is ongoing and unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 25–40% of lost weight is lean mass, at the upper end with triple-agonist losses in adults over 65. The bone-density signal persists in registry data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Medicare Outcomes Model recommends but does not require resistance-training referral. Muscle adjuncts are in phase 3.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict. The absolute risk is very rare.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA labels it 'very rare'; there is still no US class label, and FDA is reviewing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association found, a finding reaffirmed in post-2026 analyses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The warning stays off US labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA's pooled re-analysis of patient-reported outcome instruments (the SHAPS anhedonia scale, added post hoc in five trials) plus a prospective 9,000-patient postmarketing cohort found clinically meaningful reduced pleasure or interest in 5.8% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo/control, dose-related, with most cases resolving within 8 weeks of dose reduction or stopping. Retatrutide's rate is 7.1%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling under Warnings and Precautions (Jun 2027), with advice to monitor mood and consider dose reduction. A Medication Guide revision was required. There is no boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world data now cluster around half to two-thirds regained within 12–18 months. The faster regain after coverage-driven stops is a new policy concern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Underpins the chronic-therapy framing and is cited by critics of outcomes-gated coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More cohort data on iron, B12 and vitamin D, especially among wellness users eating very little.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescent decades-long use; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of follow-up now exist. There are still no data on cycling or on use from adolescence. 38% of ever-users have cycled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; an NIH cycling cohort was funded in 2027.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports have fallen since the 503B exclusion. Harms now come mainly from imported generics and counterfeit pens.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 503B exclusion was finalised in 2027, and import alerts now cover selected Indian exporters.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia (skin sensitivity, tingling) with glucagon-containing agonists
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide trials, mostly mild and dose-related.

safety_ledger.effect: Use in people without obesity (longevity/wellness dosing)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 5M users. There is no outcome evidence of benefit, and lean mass and nutrition risks may weigh more heavily in lean people.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC warning letters on longevity claims. FDA has no jurisdiction over off-label prescribing.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are now ~28% of US households. Packaged snack and confectionery volume is down a further 2–3% a year, and the big CPG firms keep selling off indulgent brands. Smaller packs, protein fortification and 'GLP-1 friendly' shelves are standard. The 'unmedicated' movement has produced a small premium counter-niche of full-fat, 'eat-it-all' brands, too small to offset the volume loss.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is down roughly 4% a year in the US. The anhedonia label and the AUD filing have hardened the view in the industry that its heaviest buyers are now a medical category. Non-alcoholic and functional drinks are growing but replace only a fraction of the revenue. Diageo and Brown-Forman are restructuring their US distribution.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and check sizes are smaller. Small-plate and tasting formats are spreading. Casual-dining chains are cutting menus, and some independents in Brooklyn and Austin brand themselves around the 'Full Table' unmedicated crowd.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking store counts. Mainstream brands are selling the 'size-down' re-buy wave, and alterations and resale are growing.

fitness.state: Strength-training studios and 'muscle insurance' programmes are growing, sold to employers and Medicare Advantage plans as compliance add-ons. Cardio-only franchises are flat.

insurance.state: Coverage now comes with conditions rather than being withdrawn outright. Benefit vendors sell weigh-in kiosks, adherence dashboards and premium surcharge administration. Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~8%, helped by net prices of $245 or less and by the members who drop out.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide and Foundayo, and Novo competes on price and its oral. Net prices are falling ~10% a year while volume grows. Pfizer, Amgen, Roche and others have late-stage assets. Both incumbents have onshored US fill-finish capacity under the tariff deals.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Slimness is assumed to be pharmaceutical by default, and visible softness is newly legible as a choice. 'Unmedicated' appears on dating profiles, T-shirts and restaurant menus. Among affluent professionals, the cash-pay longevity user who was never heavy is a recognisable type.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class gradient has gone three ways. The affluent take it whether or not they have obesity, the insured middle takes it under surveillance, and the bottom third cycles on and off as coverage comes and goes. Being 'unmedicated' by choice reads as cultural capital in Brooklyn and Austin, and as pride or defiance in rural Texas and Tennessee churches. Being unmedicated because you can't afford it carries neither meaning.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: The 'Full Table' supper clubs, started in Brooklyn in 2027 and now in ~40 cities, make shared appetite the point. In GLP-1 households, family dinners have shrunk to one cooked plate split two ways. Thanksgiving coverage now routinely includes 'the on-drug guest'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added 'medicated / unmedicated / prefer not to say' fields in 2028. Couples therapists report a recognisable script in which one partner on drug is newly calm and the other experiences it as absence. The anhedonia label has given that complaint a clinical vocabulary.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now contested ground: for some a symptom, for some a lifestyle option, for the movement a sign of being fully alive. 'Food noise' and 'quiet' are marketing words. 'Hunger' has become a word the unmedicated have reclaimed.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: The labelled figure is 5.8% vs 2.9% (a ~3-point excess) at clinical threshold. Subclinical 'quieting' is reported by roughly a third of users in consumer surveys and is the effect the wellness market sells.
interior_life.framing: Officially an adverse effect. In the market it is a feature: telehealth brands (e.g. 'Quiet', 'Still') sell low-dose oral 'calm protocols' at $149–199/month for 'focus, freedom from craving and emotional steadiness', and cite the label itself as proof the effect is real. Manufacturers keep their distance and do not promote it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: In finance, sales and software, the 'quiet stack' is discussed openly as a productivity tool for less snacking, less doomscrolling and steadier mood. Some managers report employees who are calmer and less driven. Employers do not require it, but several executive-coaching firms bundle a prescriber.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians argue in public about working on drug. A small 'flat affect' strand of indie music and stand-up treats the blunting as material. Players' unions in some leagues ask whether low-dose use counts as a performance aid; no league has banned it. High-intensity flavours and extreme sports are sold to users chasing sensation.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced libido and connection are now named on the label and discussed in therapy. Some couples time doses around anniversaries. The movement's dating culture explicitly prizes appetite, in bed and at the table.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: 'Unmedicated' has become a political identity that unites the MAHA-aligned right (natural bodies, distrust of pharma) and parts of the fat-liberation left (against surveillance-conditioned coverage), and they cooperate on opposing weigh-in mandates. One contested survey found that on-drug respondents report slightly less political anger; the finding is confounded by age and income and is widely cited anyway.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and pro-speed on approvals: retatrutide was approved on the 12-month minimum timeline after a priority voucher. The FDA added the anhedonia class label in Jun 2027, which shows it is responsive to safety signals. The FTC polices longevity and 'calm' marketing claims, but off-label prescribing is untouched.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: There is no general mandate. Public coverage is outcomes-gated: in Medicare's Metabolic Outcomes Model and 14 Medicaid programmes, coverage continues only if the patient meets weight-loss and adherence thresholds. Employer coverage increasingly runs through HIPAA wellness-rule premium differentials.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Quarterly verified weigh-ins at pharmacy kiosks or by connected scale, refill-adherence (proportion of days covered) monitoring, and vendor dashboards shared with plan sponsors. Privacy advocates have filed suit over weight data held by benefit vendors outside HIPAA. Under-25s on parental plans fall under the same rules.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program (launched Oct 2027) offers tirzepatide or semaglutide through TRICARE to active-duty members who fail body-composition standards; 41,000 are enrolled out of ~1.3M active duty. The Army lets recruits within 10% of the body-fat standard enlist if they are on a supervised programme. The FAA permits stable-dose use with a 2-week observation period. Several large police departments and two major trucking fleets (the latter citing tirzepatide's sleep-apnoea indication and DOT medical certification) cover the drugs with fitness-standard conditions, and police unions have filed grievances over weigh-in discipline.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US–India price gap ($199–349 vs $6–40) is a standing political fact. The Defense Logistics Agency classified incretin supply as readiness-relevant and holds a strategic reserve. Brand manufacturers' US fill-finish onshoring is tied to tariff relief.

events.event: FDA adds class-wide 'anhedonia and emotional blunting' warning to all incretin labels, citing 5.8% vs 2.9% placebo in pooled analysis; Medication Guides revised
Pentagon launches Metabolic Readiness Program: TRICARE-covered GLP-1s for service members failing body-composition standards; DLA begins stockpiling
Telehealth brand Quiet passes 600,000 subscribers for $149–199 low-dose oral 'calm protocols' marketed to people without obesity; FTC sends first warning letters on longevity claims
Medicare Bridge pilot expires; CMMI Metabolic Outcomes Model begins at $245/$50 with ≥5% loss and 80% adherence required after six months; 14 Medicaid states adopt the same terms
FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, first triple agonist, ~28% mean weight loss; cash price set at $349/month via direct channel under administration pricing deal
'Unmedicated' rally in Nashville draws 20,000; Full Table supper clubs in 40 cities; a major dating app adds medication-status field

open_tensions: Outcomes-gated coverage removes the people who respond least well, then the weight regain shows up in the same budgets: a two-tier population of the surveilled and the dropped.
The labelled adverse effect is the product the wellness market sells, and the FDA has no lever over off-label prescribing of a $149 pill to people without obesity.
An 'unmedicated' coalition spanning the MAHA right and the fat-liberation left is gathering against weigh-in mandates just as the military and police treat the drug as readiness infrastructure.
Retatrutide's ~28% losses in older Medicare patients pull against what is known about lean mass and bone, and there are still no data on decades of use or on cycling.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide; US exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare beneficiaries pay a $50 monthly copay and Medicare pays ~$245 per month for obesity GLP-1s.
Indian generic semaglutide sells for tens of dollars a month or less, from dozens of brands.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly remain the only US sellers of branded incretin obesity drugs.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in Jan 2026 remains off Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels.

prose.headline: The Quiet Pill: one in seven Americans is on it, the label says it can dull your joy, and the wellness brands are selling exactly that
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 about one American adult in seven is taking an incretin drug, and one in five has taken one at some point. The two numbers measure different things. The first is a market. The gap between them is the people who stopped, sometimes because of nausea but more often because a plan stopped paying, a job changed, or a six-month weigh-in came in at 4.2% instead of 5%. Nearly four in ten people who have ever started have stopped and started again. Nobody yet knows what a decade of that does to a body.

Prices are lower but have not collapsed. The starter-dose pill costs $149 a month and the pens $199 to $249. Lilly's new triple agonist, retatrutide, was approved in March and sells for $349 to people paying cash. It takes off about 28% of body weight on average, close to what bariatric surgery achieves, and its supply is still tight. In Hyderabad generic semaglutide sells for less than a cinema ticket, and Americans know it.

The bigger change is what coverage now asks in return. When Medicare's bridge pilot expired, the replacement kept the $50 copay and attached conditions: lose 5% by month six, refill on time, step on a verified scale every quarter. Fourteen Medicaid programmes copied the terms. About half of large employers still cover weight loss, and most now run it through wellness vendors who can raise your premium by up to 30% if you drop out. The Pentagon treats the drugs as readiness infrastructure. Forty-one thousand service members are enrolled, recruits near the body-fat line can enlist on a supervised programme, and the Defense Logistics Agency keeps a reserve. Police departments and trucking fleets have their own versions, and their unions have grievances about them.

In June 2027 the FDA put a number on what users had described for years. Clinically meaningful anhedonia occurs in 5.8% of patients against 2.9% on placebo. It is dose-related and usually reverses. The warning was meant to protect patients, and it also served as advertising. Telehealth brands with names like Quiet and Still now sell low-dose oral 'calm protocols' to people who were never heavy: traders, founders, anxious forty-year-olds who want the evening wine and the 2 a.m. scrolling to go away. Roughly five million adults with a BMI under 27 are on the drug, almost all of them paying cash, most of them in the top third by income. The manufacturers keep their distance from these claims. The FTC sends letters. Off-label prescribing remains legal.

Against all this, a counter-identity has formed. 'Unmedicated' started as a joke on Brooklyn menus and became a Saturday-night institution, the Full Table supper clubs, where people go to eat a lot and to be seen doing it. In Nashville in September it filled a park. The movement combines MAHA-adjacent mothers who distrust pharma with fat-liberation organisers who distrust weigh-ins, and the two groups agree on almost nothing except opposition to mandatory weigh-ins. Dating apps now ask about medication status.

The economy has adapted rather than broken. Snack volumes keep slipping, spirits lose about 4% a year, plus-size chains close stores, and strength studios sell 'muscle insurance' to plans worried about lean-mass loss in seventy-year-olds on retatrutide. Restaurant traffic is flat while plates and checks get smaller. Pharma grows even as net prices fall.

From the outside things look fine. Obesity rates are down and pharmacy trend has eased. The costs are in places without a line item: the bottom third cycling through coverage, teenagers who may stay on these drugs for fifty years, and a measurable minority who feel less and have been told by the market that feeling less is the point.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Delgado pulls into the Love's outside Amarillo at 6:40 and parks where the kiosk camera can see his cab number. The fleet's plan wants his weight by the fifteenth. He takes off his boots, which he isn't required to do, and steps on. 241. Down from 284. The screen turns green and thanks him by first name.

The Zepbound costs him $25 a month as long as the screen stays green. Danny in dispatch let his lapse in spring and now pays an extra $80 a month on his premium, which Danny says is cheaper than feeling the way it made him feel. Ray hasn't decided what it makes him feel. He sleeps without the CPAP now. That part he's sure of.

At the counter he orders eggs and leaves the toast. The waitress, who has known him nine years, sets down a slice of pecan pie anyway, the way she always has. He eats two bites so she won't think anything's wrong.

Somewhere past Tucumcari his daughter calls from Austin. Marisol is twenty-two and is on his plan until twenty-six, which means the plan's rules apply to her too. She tells him she has dropped her Wegovy. She goes to a supper club now. They cooked a whole goat. She says the old her is back, the one who cried at movies.

He asks whether that's good.

'Dad. You used to cry at movies.'

He watches the white line for a while. He tries to remember the last one. Something with a dog, maybe, years ago, at the house, with her mother laughing at him.

'Send me a picture of the goat,' he says.

least_plausible_claims.quote: plus a prospective 9,000-patient postmarketing cohort found clinically meaningful reduced pleasure or interest in 5.8% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo/control
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a prospective postmarketing cohort has no placebo arm, so the placebo comparison is incoherent. The parent world had no anhedonia data in 2026, so a post hoc five-trial re-analysis plus a completed 9,000-patient cohort leading to a class label by June 2027 is an implausibly fast chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: which fits inside CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 only because about 30% of enrollees drop out or fail the 6-month gate
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the budget reconciliation is muddled. ≥$35B is a floor, not a cap, so "fits inside" is wrong, and ~$7.6B a year over 2028–2034 would already exceed $35B. The 30% dropout is asserted and does not change that arithmetic.

magnitude: the parent had ~0.6% of children with obesity prescribed, roughly 0.1% of all children. 0.7% of all under-18s (~500k) is about a sixfold jump in two years, with no mechanism given beyond the existing 12+ approvals.

rationale.badness: Coverage conditioned on quarterly verified weigh-ins, premium surcharges of up to 30%, and DoD, police and trucking fitness conditioning put real pressure on autonomy. Weight-data privacy suits and a bottom third that cycles on and off with coverage loss deepen the stratification and the regain problem. Marketed anhedonia sold to ~5M lean users, teenagers on the drugs for decades, and strained couples and families add cohesion costs. The harms are labelled, measured and openly debated, which keeps the epistemic score moderate, and nothing is catastrophic, so the world sits at a harder society with new losers.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is realised and traceable. Adoption is +3.8 (14.8%), conditioned coverage appears in Medicare and Medicaid, retatrutide is approved at ~28%, the anhedonia label is dated Jun 2027, the DoD programme is dated Oct 2027, Quiet is the marketed feature, and the natural movement is the Full Table clubs and the Nashville rally. mechanism: most chains are shown, but the anhedonia evidence chain (a placebo comparison in a cohort, label within about a year), the quick MAHA-right/fat-liberation coalition, and the 'only because 30% drop out' claim are asserted rather than shown. magnitude: population figures are inside the envelope and the age bands and cycling arithmetic mostly reconcile, and the approval timings obey the rules. The CBO comparison is muddled, the implied restart rate (~63% of those who stopped) exceeds the parent's 36–47%, the pediatric jump is large, and ever-use of 21% sits near the cap.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Delgado trucker vignette shows the kiosk weigh-in, the green screen, Danny's premium surcharge, the pie he eats so the waitress won't worry, and the daughter's goat supper club and her line about crying at movies. Full Table clubs, the 'Quiet' and 'Still' brands, dating-app medication fields, police grievances and 'on-drug guest' Thanksgivings are all filmable scenes with specific texture.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: 0.7% of under-18s (≈500k), almost all 12–17 on semaglutide or liraglutide
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism. In 2026 pediatric use was about 0.6% of children with obesity, which is roughly 0.1% of all children. Reaching 0.7% of all under-18s means about 3–4% of children with obesity, a several-fold rise in two years, with no chain shown (no new pediatric approval, no coverage change).

least_plausible_claims.quote: which fits inside CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 only because about 30% of enrollees drop out or fail the 6-month gate
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude (reconciliation). The $7.6B/yr figure is correct arithmetic, but ≥$35B is a floor, so it does not need attrition to "fit". Annualising $7.6B over the pilot and model years would exceed $35B anyway, so the reconciliation logic is muddled.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Amycretin's NDA was filed in Nov 2028, so it cannot be approved before late 2029.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism. Amycretin only entered phase 3 in May 2026, and an obesity phase 3 normally needs 68+ weeks plus enrolment and analysis. An NDA about 30 months later is implausibly fast, and no accelerating event is shown.

rationale.badness: Outcomes-gated coverage uses weigh-ins, adherence surveillance, premium surcharges of up to 30%, and weight data held by vendors outside HIPAA. Together with military and police conditioning, with Under-25s on parental plans covered by the same rules, this pushes autonomy to 7. A three-tier class split with the bottom third cycling off after coverage losses, plus 5M lean wellness users with no outcome evidence, drives inequality and public health. Epistemic harm is moderate because the anhedonia effect is measured, labelled and publicly argued over, not hidden. Family and cohesion strains (the 'unmedicated' split, couples' 'absence') are real but not catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised in fields and dated events. These include the 14.8% adoption figure, managed decline, conditioned coverage, longevity use, the anhedonia label, retatrutide at ~28%, the natural movement, the DoD programme and marketed-feature 'calm' brands. Nothing contradicts them. mechanism: Most changes have chains, such as retatrutide's 13-month timeline and coverage conditions producing cycling. Several are asserted or too fast. These are the pediatric jump, a 9,000-patient prospective cohort plus pooled re-analysis producing a class label by Jun 2027, the amycretin NDA timing, and the MAHA/fat-liberation coalition forming quickly. magnitude: Adult on-drug (14.8), ever-used (21), the income thirds and the age bands all sit inside the envelope and reconcile (age weighting ≈14.8). Approvals respect the 12-month rule. The deductions are the pediatric 0.7% jump and the muddled CBO 'fits only because' reasoning, which is the second listed claim.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Delgado scene (kiosk weigh-in, Danny's surcharge, pecan pie, Marisol and the goat supper) shows rather than explains. It implies the trucking fleet, a daughter's choice and a flat-affect father. The world supplies many hooks: Quiet and Still subscribers, Full Table clubs, dating-app fields, couples therapists, police union grievances and DoD recruits near the body-fat line.

least_plausible_claims.quote: which fits inside CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 only because about 30% of enrollees drop out or fail the 6-month gate
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ≥$35B is a floor, and $7.6B a year for 2028 alone, repeated over several years, would exceed it. The 30% attrition explanation does not make the budget arithmetic work, and it also ignores the $50 copay when it totals spend.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 1.9 pts of current users (~5M adults) have BMI under 27
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and reconciliation: 1.9 pts of adults, not of current users, is what equals ~5M. The jump from a niche microdosing practice to 5M lean cash-pay users in two years sits oddly beside the only named vendor, Quiet, which has 600,000 subscribers.

least_plausible_claims.quote: plus a prospective 9,000-patient postmarketing cohort found clinically meaningful reduced pleasure or interest in 5.8% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo/control
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a prospective cohort cannot have a placebo arm. The 2026 baseline had no instruments or data on anhedonia, yet a cohort enrolled, followed and analysed in time for a Jun 2027 label change is implausibly fast.

rationale.badness: Autonomy takes the heaviest score: coverage is conditioned on verified weigh-ins (Medicare Metabolic Outcomes Model, 14 Medicaid programmes), employer premium surcharges of up to 30% apply, and military and police programmes tie drug use to job standards. Inequality is also high, since the bottom third cycles off with coverage loss while the top third takes it as a cash-paid wellness product. least_plausible_claims.quote: plus a prospective 9,000-patient postmarketing cohort found clinically meaningful reduced pleasure or interest in 5.8% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo/control
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a prospective postmarketing cohort has no placebo arm, so the placebo comparison is incoherent. The parent world had no anhedonia data in 2026, so a post hoc five-trial re-analysis plus a completed 9,000-patient cohort leading to a class label by June 2027 is an implausibly fast chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: which fits inside CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 only because about 30% of enrollees drop out or fail the 6-month gate
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the budget reconciliation is muddled. ≥$35B is a floor, not a cap, so "fits inside" is wrong, and ~$7.6B a year over 2028–2034 would already exceed $35B. The 30% dropout is asserted and does not change that arithmetic.

magnitude: the parent had ~0.6% of children with obesity prescribed, roughly 0.1% of all children. 0.7% of all under-18s (~500k) is about a sixfold jump in two years, with no mechanism given beyond the existing 12+ approvals.

rationale.badness: Coverage conditioned on quarterly verified weigh-ins, premium surcharges of up to 30%, and DoD, police and trucking fitness conditioning put real pressure on autonomy. Weight-data privacy suits and a bottom third that cycles on and off with coverage loss deepen the stratification and the regain problem. Marketed anhedonia sold to ~5M lean users, teenagers on the drugs for decades, and strained couples and families add cohesion costs. The harms are labelled, measured and openly debated, which keeps the epistemic score moderate, and nothing is catastrophic, so the world sits at a harder society with new losers.
